- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially in late horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often holds too high; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast by 1–3% in 5–7 day window.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment > 0.70 over last 7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., +3%+ per day for 3+ days), model often lags; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for next 5–7 days.
